title: AI Testing: What It Is, Types, Strategy and Platform
description: AI testing means using AI to plan, write, run and maintain software tests, and testing AI systems themselves. Types, strategy and how to start.

sections.head: What AI testing covers today

items: Pick the risk
Start with the flows or AI features where a failure costs the most: checkout, sign-in, a support bot.
Write acceptance criteria
State what must be true in plain English. These criteria decide pass or fail, not the AI.
Generate and review tests
Let an agent such as KaneAI draft the tests; an engineer reviews them before they gate a release.
Run on real conditions
Run app tests on real browsers and devices, and agent tests with simulated users at volume.
Track and tighten
Watch flaky tests and failure clusters; add criteria where bugs escaped.

sections.head: Types of AI testing

rows: Hallucination
Answers that state facts not found in your sources
Share of answers with an unsupported claim
Grounding
Answers that ignore or misquote the documents the agent was given
Answer checked against the retrieved source text
Bias
Different quality or tone for different user groups
Same scenario run with varied personas, results compared
Task completion
Conversations that end without doing the job: refund, booking, reset
Share of scenarios that reach the expected end state
sections.src: Agent Testing runs these scenarios with simulated users and scores every conversation: see Agent Testing. The four measures map to the Measure function of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), which asks teams to test AI systems for validity, reliability, fairness and safety before deployment.
sections.head: How to test an AI system
body: Inputs, then scenarios, then scoring, then a verdict. Score each answer on the four measures below; a release passes only when every measure meets the bar you set.

rows: Letting the AI decide pass or fail
A model grading its own work hides regressions

Real users phrase things in ways a short list never covers
Run hundreds of varied scenarios, including hostile and off-topic ones
Testing once before launch
Model, prompt and data changes shift behaviour after release
Re-run the same scenario set on every model or prompt change

sections.head: Where AI testing happens on TestMu AI

items.q: Which metrics show whether an AI agent is ready to ship?
items.a: Track four: hallucination rate (answers with unsupported claims), grounding (answers that match your source documents), bias (quality differences across user personas) and task completion (conversations that reach the expected end state). Set a bar for each before testing, and block the release if any measure misses it.
AI testing is using artificial intelligence to plan, write, run and maintain software tests. The term also covers testing AI systems, such as chatbots and voice agents, for correctness and safety.

items.q: How do you test an AI system?
items.a: Define the behaviour you expect, run many realistic conversations or inputs against it, and score the answers for accuracy, grounding and policy. Agent Testing on TestMu AI automates this.

items.q: What are the types of AI testing?
items.a: Common types are AI-driven test authoring, self-healing maintenance, visual AI comparison, test analytics, and evaluation of AI agents and models.

items.q: Which AI testing tool should I start with?
items.a: For web and mobile apps start with KaneAI or Kane CLI. For chat, voice or phone agents start with Agent Testing. The AI testing platform brings both together.

items.q: Does AI testing replace test automation frameworks?
items.a: No. Teams keep Selenium, Playwright and Appium suites and run them on TestMu AI, and use AI agents for new coverage and maintenance.
